design_rules.rule: A stable design must meet the declared phase margin and gain margin at the worst-case load and temperature, not only the nominal closed-loop gain.
design_rules.check: phase margin >= acceptance and gain margin >= acceptance

provenance.citation: Texas Instruments Op Amps for Everyone

design_rules.rule: If the margin fails, compute a compensation that the model supports and re-evaluate the loop; do not declare stability from a nominal gain.
design_rules.check: compensation raises the modeled margin above acceptance

provenance.citation: Texas Instruments Op Amps for Everyone

manufacturing_rules.rule: Control PCB parasitics at the inverting node and the output load because they move the poles that determine stability.
manufacturing_rules.check: layout extraction or measurement of critical parasitics

provenance.citation: Analog layout practice

failure_modes.cause: insufficient phase margin from output/input capacitance or unmodeled poles
failure_modes.detection: loop-gain injection and step-response measurement at worst-case load

worked_cases.description: A 100 dB, 10 Hz first-pole op-amp with a 1 MHz second pole, 100 ohm output resistance, 1 uF load, 1 nF input capacitance and noise gain 10 has negative phase margin.

expected.name: crossover_frequency
expected.note: numerical crossover of the declared loop

expected.name: phase_margin
expected.note: negative margin: unstable under the small-signal model

provenance.citation: Closed-form loop-gain evaluation of the declared fixture
provenance.note: Inputs are synthetic fixture values, not a device datasheet.

counterexamples.claim: A closed-loop gain of 10 proves stability.
counterexamples.refutation: Gain is a DC algebra ratio. The loop can still have negative phase margin when the output and input capacitances add poles; the model produces a negative margin for a nominal gain of 10.

provenance.citation: Texas Instruments Op Amps for Everyone

known_traps.trap: Concluding stability from the nominal closed-loop gain without the load, input capacitance and loop phase.
known_traps.why_shallow_fails: The arithmetic for gain is correct but the stability question is about loop phase at crossover, which capacitive load and input capacitance change.
known_traps.guard: Require loop data and compute phase/gain margin; refuse or report unavailable when the capacitances are missing.
